newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea proposes to raise tax on local liquor.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea proposes to raise tax on local liquor.

text.p: South Korea has proposed raising taxes on the nation's popular liquor, called soju, to meet demands from the European Union to balance tax rates with imported whisky, the finance ministry said on Monday.

The EU filed an action with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in April, requesting consultations over South Korea's purported discriminatory tax regime on liquors. The consultations started in Geneva on May 29.
South Korea suggested increasing tax on soju, with an alcohol strength of 25 percent, to 62.5 percent from the current 35 percent.
It also proposed raising tax on soju with an alcohol content of 40 percent to 100 percent from 50 percent. But it recommended maintaining its 100 percent tax on whisky.
The 10 percent education tax on soju and 30 percent education tax on whisky, brandy and vodka, would be adjusted to a uniform rate of 20 to 30 percent, it said.
Seoul proposed to gradually implement the new taxation system over the next three to four years, the ministry said.
EU officials said they would give their position after reviewing the South Korean proposal.
